newsitem.title: USA: Galaxy sees $17-$20 mln sales for FY97.
newsitem.headline: Galaxy sees $17-$20 mln sales for FY97.

text.p: Galaxy Foods Co said on Monday it expected to have annualized net sales of about $17 million to $20 million for the year ended March 31, 1997, compared to sales of $3.9 million in the prior fiscal year.

The company said gains were due to the introduction of new products to health food stores and supermarkets in the United States, increased export sales and an increase in business from the franchise buying group for Taco Bell.
Galaxy also said it aimed to achieve 17 percent profit margins to the bottom line by the end of calendar 1997.
But Galaxy said it had significant overtime expenditures while hiring and training new production crews, and increased marketing expenses for new product introductions.
"These extra expenses will impact our October - December 1996 quarter and unfortunately will slightly delay our profitability," the company said.
Galaxy said sales were helped by the optimization of its new slicing machine, which came on line in October 1995.
It said its second so-called individually wrapped "hot pack" slicing machine, which more than tripled the company's production capacity, would be on line in January 1997.
The machine puts cheese in individually wrapped slices.
This new machine was 55 percent sold out and Galaxy said it expected the machine to be operating at full capacity within the first six months of 1997.

"We are also beginning to mature several of our other production lines (soft cheeses, grated cheeses, shredded cheeses and others) and expect to post significant growth of these products during 1997," Galaxy said.
